summary: Speeding remains a significant road safety concern across Toronto, putting pedestrians, cyclists, and motorists at risk. The City needs additional tools that allow us to respond quickly to speeding concerns. Rubber speed bumps provide a practical and cost-effective option. Already used on Toronto laneways and on various roadway types in municipalities across Ontario, they can be installed more quickly than permanent speed humps and removed if determined to be unnecessary. Expanding their use would give the City greater flexibility to address speeding and improve road safety while permanent traffic calming measures are planned.
decided: City Council on July 29 and 30, 2026, referred Item MM43.16 to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee.

motions.desc: Two-Thirds required - MM43.16 - Waive the referral
